paragraphs: Every day, as part of her walk around the farm, Bessie the cow visits her favorite pasture, which has N flowers (all colorful daisies) labeled 1…N lined up in a row (1 ≤ N ≤ 100). Flower i has pᵢ petals (1 ≤ pᵢ ≤ 1000).

As a budding photographer, Bessie decides to take several photos of these flowers. In particular, for every pair of flowers (i, j) satisfying 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ N, Bessie takes a photo of all flowers from flower i to flower j (including i and j).

Bessie later looks at these photos and notices that some of these photos have an "average flower" — a flower that has P petals, where P is the exact average number of petals among all flowers in the photo.
How many of Bessie's photos have an average flower?
inputFormat: The first line of input contains N.
The second line contains N space-separated integers p₁ … pₙ.
outputFormat: Please print out the number of photos that have an average flower.

sampleExplanation.title: Sample Analysis
sampleExplanation.detail: Every single-flower photo (4 of them) trivially has an average flower. Among multi-flower ranges, (1, 2) has petals [1, 1] with average 1, and (2, 4) has petals [1, 2, 3] with average 2 (matching flower 3).

hints.title: Small Constraints Allow Complete Search
hints.body: Since N ≤ 100, there are at most N(N + 1)/2 ≈ 5,050 photos (i, j). Even an O(N³) algorithm checks at most ~500,000 elements, which is tiny!

hints.title: Avoid Floating-Point Precision Bugs
hints.body: Instead of computing average = sum / len as a float, check divisibility with integers! Flower k in [i..j] equals the exact average if and only if p[k] * (j − i + 1) == totalSum.

editorial.summary: Enumerate every subarray [i..j], compute its sum S and length L = j − i + 1, and check if any element p[k] in [i..j] satisfies p[k] · L == S using exact integer arithmetic.
editorial.complexity: Time: O(N³) or O(N²)  |  Space: O(N)

solutions.python:
import sys

def solve():
    data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
    n = data[0]
    p = data[1:1 + n]
    ans = 0
    for i in range(n):
        total = 0
        seen = set()
        for j in range(i, n):
            total += p[j]
            seen.add(p[j])
            length = j - i + 1
            if total % length == 0 and (total // length) in seen:
                ans += 1
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
